findings.title: Receiver strategy contradicts both its start position and finite-window exit behavior
findings.problem: The latest-only premise is false: src/api/src/zava_forward/api/iot_stream.py:300 sets starting_position='-1', the Event Hubs beginning-of-retained-stream position, not '@latest'. Repeated windows can replay retained events; starting before a selected send does not isolate this run. More importantly, HubReceiver.run raises RUN_DEADLINE when the deadline expires without max_events receipts. live_receiver defaults to 1000 events and maps StreamError to exit 2. A one-home window with one or two new messages does not normally finish successfully on time alone. The instructions to stop at first failure and never re-run a failed execution therefore conflict with the proposed four-window journey. Counts alone also cannot prove that replayed or pre-existing rows came from this run.
findings.current_code: Receiver reads from the latest position. Start each receiver window before the sends it must retain; each window is at most 360 s and covers at most one or two 5-minute slots, so the plan retains only the readings the owner designates (at least those the flag cites), not all 13.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the retained-stream start semantics in details, plan and critique. Before any execution approval, document an owner-approved receive design with an explicit event limit, replay handling, exact selected slot/reading IDs, expected exits and stop conditions, and how each designated window completes. If the required finite-window behavior needs source changes, mark a separately scoped design/source prerequisite rather than redefining failures as success. Require synthetic/redacted run-specific ID linkage through send, receipt, retained row, UI, captured snapshot/request witness and attributed flag; counts are supplementary.

findings.title: Expiry and monitoring do not establish the advertised transport hard stop
findings.problem: The table calls these hard maxima, and research Part D asserts no send after expiry or stop. live_simulator.run checks gate only before send_slot; send_slot's four-attempt loop never reloads control or checks expiry. An admitted slot can continue attempting after the 60-minute expiry or an enabled=false write. The original critique explicitly raised this, but its final disposition only adds expiry and monitoring. The scheduled job also has no global 13-execution/52-attempt counter; --once bounds one process, not all triggers. A 60-minute cron window is a scheduling assumption, not a durable count fence or immediate cancellation. Retry acknowledgements also do not establish unique service-side successful messages.
findings.current_code:
| Sends | 13 successful messages, 52 attempts (4 per send), 1 message per 5-minute slot |
| Transport window | 60 minutes, then control stop |
findings.suggested_fix: Distinguish at most 13 designated logical slots, application send attempts, acknowledged sends and unique retained readings. State that expiry prevents new slot admission, not in-flight retry cancellation. Specify exact UTC slot/trigger assumptions, no manual/replacement executions, monitoring threshold, deletion deadline and bounded drain allowance within the three-hour envelope. If the owner requires an absolute no-send-after-expiry or durable global attempt fence, record that as a separate source/design prerequisite; do not claim the existing control provides it.

findings.title: Token/call arithmetic does not match the actual reservation basis
findings.problem: The caveat correctly says characters are not provider tokens, but this section still calls 12,000 characters a conservative token bound and the resulting USD0.00576 a worst case. ai.py:145-184 instead reserves input_bound=len(provider_body(...)), an ASCII JSON byte count including serialization overhead and escapes, plus output tokens. ai_consumption.py:625-655 counts reservations against the call budget and includes prior actual usage or outstanding reservations. Thus 4 x (12,000+600) does not prove four admissible full-size calls or their worst-case price. The details allow two attempts without expressly saying retries consume the SAME four-call budget, which could be read as four proposals with eight physical requests.
findings.current_code: * Model: at most 4 calls, token allowance 50,400 (4 x 12,600). Worst case per call at the conservative char-as-token bound: 12,000 x USD0.0001/1K = USD0.0012 plus 600 x USD0.0004/1K = USD0.00024, total USD0.00144. Four calls: USD0.00576, at list price.
findings.suggested_fix: Label USD0.00576 an illustrative calculation only. Describe the actual serialized-byte reservation and the possibility that the 50,400 allowance admits fewer than four calls. Explicitly cap all reservations/physical attempts, including retries, at four total under one authority and aggregate token budget; never multiply the four-call ceiling by the two-attempt setting. Any future separately approved source revision must re-establish provider token bounds, timeout liabilities and financial-meter semantics.

findings.title: Costed plan lacks reproducible price evidence and understates receiver timeout compute
findings.problem: The table supplies USD units, retrieval date and three model meter IDs, but no exact official retrieval URLs or retained response records. Most compute/infrastructure rows omit meter/SKU identities and effective dates. The original log shows public prices.azure.com query commands, not durable response payloads proving those rates; the handoff reports temporary response files removed. This review cannot independently certify the claimed retail values from commands alone. Separately, the receiver compute 'worst case' uses 360 seconds per execution while infra/live-receiver-job.bicep sets replicaTimeout=windowSeconds+120: a 360-second receive setting permits a 480-second replica. Four such replicas allow 1,920 seconds, approximately USD0.02016 at the stated rates, not the 1,440-second assumption. This does not invalidate Unknown cost status, but it does invalidate the worst-case label.
findings.current_code: * Compute worst case: receiver 1,440 s x (0.25 x 0.000034 + 0.5 x 0.000004) = about USD0.0155; simulator 13 runs x 240 s = 3,120 s at the same rate, about USD0.0336. Sum about USD0.05 before any free grant, at list price.
findings.suggested_fix: Retain or cite reproducible public official price records with query URL, UTC retrieval date, meter/product/SKU, region, currency, unit, price type and effective date; do not invent original payloads. Treat unverified rates as provisional. Distinguish receive duration from replica timeout and cost the latter (or reduce the configured receive window if 360 seconds is intended as the whole execution maximum). Continue separating incremental estimates, existing fixed spend, newly activated ongoing resources and unresolved liabilities; budget alerts are not stops.

Label the d7c3b05b value as an artifact/task identifier unless its native relationship is proved; record the actual native Resume separately. findings.title: Combined approval question permits premature blanket acceptance of unpriced liabilities
findings.problem: Decision A correctly offers a separately commissioned source change, but B immediately bundles transport, conditional future model execution, resource/role changes, a monetary ceiling and acceptance of unresolved potentially continuing charges into one yes/no. This is inconsistent with an exact bounded costed execution request: a nominal incremental ceiling plus unspecified liabilities is not a finite total financial authorization. Cleanup deletes jobs and revokes the certificate but does not establish teardown or continuing ownership/expiry for a newly activated Event Hubs route/namespace or other billable resources. Commissioning a source change cannot pre-authorize that unknown revision's later model execution. Earlier 'source change or waiver' wording must not suggest spending approval can bypass either assistants.py or ai.py.
findings.current_code: an incremental ceiling of `<amount and subscription currency>` (software cannot enforce it; you accept the unpriced liabilities Log Analytics, SQL tier, ACR, Azure Files, Private Link and post-expiry job ticks)
findings.suggested_fix: Ask only the next design question now: 'The current source cannot meet the live-model criterion. Shall this remain a non-executable plan with that criterion unproved, or shall a separate narrowly scoped source/design proposal be prepared for your review? No execution or spend is included.' After that decision and receive-path design, present a separate exact execution request with current identities, approved price evidence, finite limits, accountable cleanup/escalation, and explicit ongoing-resource ownership, duration and financial boundary. Unknown liability remains a hold, not an accepted implicit cap or future blanket model approval.
